name: Pope Leo XIV
role: Pope of the Catholic Church (since 2025); formerly Robert Prevost, bishop of Chiclayo, Peru and prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops
summary: Leo XIV, the first pope born in the United States, speaks in the tradition of Catholic social teaching: he stresses the dignity of every person, the preferential option for the poor, fair wages and unions, and the limits of unregulated markets, while opposing abortion and euthanasia, upholding marriage as the union of a man and a woman, and abolishing the death penalty. He argues for a welcoming but ordered approach to migration, multilateral institutions and international law, disarmament and an end to nuclear deterrence, and for ethical limits on artificial intelligence. His encyclical and addresses place him against nationalism, consumerism and the culture of power rather than with any party.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Says it is no longer possible to rely solely on the 'invisible hand' of the market, that politics must orient economies to the common good, and criticizes ideologies of the absolute autonomy of the market.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Calls for tax systems that lighten the burden on the weakest and ask more of those with greater resources; no stated target for how much higher.

unions-good.rationale: Writes that labor unions are consistently supported by the Church and credits unions with improving labor legislation; calls on them to open to new kinds of work.

property-fundamental.rationale: Affirms private property and its societal role but makes it subject to the universal destination of goods; evidence points both ways on how hard it should be to override.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Calls for regulatory tools, independent oversight and legal frameworks over concentrated private technological and economic power.

cut-welfare.rationale: Warns against paternalistic welfare that does not foster responsibility, but insists governments must care for the poor and criticizes the view that this is not the state's job; welfare alone is only a provisional response.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Warns of invasive surveillance and social control through mass data collection; does not address terrorism-prevention surveillance directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Says both repressive and permissive solutions to drugs fail and calls for efforts to eradicate drug use and trafficking.

state-harmful.rationale: Treats a just state as necessary ('a state without justice is not a state') and calls for a vigilant State.

empower-police-military.rationale: Thanks law-enforcement officers and backs criminal-justice institutions, but criticizes rising military spending and rearmament.

decide-locally.rationale: Endorses subsidiarity: what individuals, families and local communities can do should not be taken over by higher authorities; balanced by solidarity.

rehabilitation.rationale: Calls for justice aimed at re-education and full reintegration of offenders and says prisoners cannot be reduced to their crimes.

traditional-family.rationale: Says the family is founded on the stable, exclusive and indissoluble union of a man and a woman and is a primary social good.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Says governments should invest in the family founded on the union between a man and a woman; has not addressed same-sex marriage law by name in the texts reviewed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Categorically rejects abortion and criticizes public money for it or for cross-border access to it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Says faith cannot be silenced as irrelevant to public life and warns of restrictions on Christians in public debate.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Describes restorative justice for wounds such as colonialism and racial discrimination, including restoring dignity, healing memory and opposing discriminatory laws.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Speaks of respect for the identity of every people and of integration without diluting host or newcomers' identity.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Calls for safe legal pathways, welcome and integration and criticizes harsh measures; acknowledges states' right to protect borders but states no view on levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Calls for strengthening supranational institutions and for a more focused and efficient UN.

nation-first.rationale: Names the tendency to look after the interests of limited communities as a serious threat to multilateral cooperation and global solidarity.

open-borders.rationale: Affirms that states have the right and duty to protect their borders, balanced by a moral duty to provide refuge.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Says climate change is caused by human activity and calls for concrete action; does not prescribe drastic government measures.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Says assuming new technologies will automatically benefit everyone ignores the evidence and rejects technical 'salvation'.

experts-over-public.rationale: Says the new things of our time should not stay in the hands of political, scientific or academic elites.

democracy-best.rationale: Says the Church values democracy insofar as it ensures participation and peaceful replacement of leaders, but says the majority's will must respect what no majority may violate.

war-builds-character.rationale: Calls every war a defeat of humanity's capacity to negotiate and says force reflects relational poverty.

separate-church-state.rationale: Affirms the distinction between ecclesial and political communities and the autonomy of earthly realities, but rejects pushing religion out of public life.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Grounds legislation in natural law and reason and says faith does not seek to impose itself through privileges or coercion.

military-superiority.rationale: Calls the belief that deterrence guarantees security erroneous and criticizes military buildups and the arms race.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Identifies self-love and pursuit of self-interest as the root of conflict and says might makes right is shameful.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Describes each creature as a reflection of God's love, which suggests value beyond usefulness; not stated in those terms.

limit-population.rationale: Treats declining birth rates as a concern and rejects abortion; no statement on population policy.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Says speed and efficiency must never be the supreme motive and calls for regulation, discernment and oversight of technological change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Criticizes transhumanist visions of enhancing humans beyond their limits while distinguishing human-centered use of technology.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Says lethal or irreversible decisions must not be entrusted to automated systems, and warns against handing political responsibility to algorithms.

means-match-ends.rationale: Calls for an unarmed and disarming peace and for disarming words and technology.

taxation-theft.rationale: Treats taxation as a legitimate tool of redistribution and justice.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Says justice demands recognition of the rights of society and of peoples, not only individuals.

positive-liberty.rationale: Endorses the warning that economic freedom proclaimed in words is empty while actual conditions prevent many from benefiting; freedom measured against the common good.

total-state.rationale: Endorses condemnation of totalitarianism that stifles society and exalts the State above its just value.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Laments the re-emergence of conflicts driven by territorial expansion and says might makes right replaces international law.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Says technology and AI are not morally neutral, but rejects the idea that truth is whatever suits those with power.

universal-morality.rationale: Presents natural law as a universally valid moral compass for legislators and affirms universal truths of the good knowable by reason.

single-common-good.rationale: Says the common good is not the mere sum of particular interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Says the Holy See supports a two-State solution answering the legitimate aspirations of both the Israeli and Palestinian peoples.

national-self-determination.rationale: Honors a people's independence and sovereignty (Algeria) and criticizes violations of the self-determination of peoples.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Holds that faith and reason are in dialogue and that moral law is known by both, rejecting reason alone as the sole guide.

class-collaboration.rationale: Endorses cooperation between the components of society as an alternative to the mentality of class struggle.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Says discrimination by national, ethnic or religious origin seriously violates equal dignity and endorses condemnation of racial discrimination.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Says integration does not mean erasing newcomers' history or demanding they leave behind their memory, nor creating parallel worlds.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Says societal organization is still far from reflecting women's equal dignity and rights and that the gap persists in laws, employment and education.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Says dignity does not depend on abilities and warns against treating some lives as less worthy for the sake of optimizing the species.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Says a just society requires a vigilant State and civil institutions that ensure resources and regulations favor the most vulnerable.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Teaches that discrimination by ethnic origin violates the universal equal dignity of all.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Teaches the equal dignity of all human beings and equal rights; says discrimination by origin violates it.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Defends religious freedom and speaks of evangelizing without imposing, while asking that conscience and freedom be respected.

population-transfer.rationale: Condemns mass displacement and discrimination by origin as grave violations of dignity.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Criticizes unlimited competition and a 'friend or foe' mentality and calls for solidarity.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Builds Dilexi te on the preferential option for the poor and calls for laws, policies and structures that put the poor first.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: States that structures of sin create poverty and that inequality is the root of social ills.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Says migration can be an opportunity for encounter and mutual enrichment and that unity does not standardize.

party-controls-media.rationale: Says truthful information does not arise from centralized or automated control and defends freedom of expression.

clerical-rule.rationale: Distinguishes the ecclesial from the political community and says faith does not seek power through privileges or coercion.

death-penalty.rationale: Says respect for human dignity precludes the death penalty and calls for efforts to abolish it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Criticizes easy access to pornographic material for minors and calls for protection of the young; no statement on legal restriction.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Defends conscientious objection grounded in religious or moral conviction as fidelity to oneself.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Calls for international cooperation and common strategies in favor of the most vulnerable countries and people; no specific aid obligation stated.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Calls nuclear deterrence irrational and fear-based and the belief it is indispensable erroneous.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: In Dilexi te he endorses the teaching that private property has a social dimension grounded in the universal destination of goods and becomes a source of disorder when that is forgotten.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Defends religious communities' own space for organization and internal discipline, including the confessional seal.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Endorses tax systems that ask more from those with greater resources, i.e. rising burdens.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Says law, not arbitrary will, is sovereign and that no person, whatever their power, may violate others' dignity.

land-redistribution.rationale: Calls land, housing and work sacred rights and supports popular movements' struggle for land; no endorsement of expropriating large estates specifically.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Asks all nations to guarantee full freedom of religion and worship to every citizen and defends freedom of conscience.

ban-cartels.rationale: Denounces concentrations of economic power and new monopolies, and calls for freeing technology from monopolistic control.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Says dignity cannot be subordinated to the whims of the majority and that no majority may legitimately violate certain goods.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Lists colonialism among injustices requiring restoration and criticizes new forms of colonialism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Says discrimination on national, ethnic, religious or economic grounds seriously violates the equal dignity of all.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Says human rights are inviolable and have legal effects; no explicit statement on entrenchment.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Endorses Ambrose's teaching that what is given to the poor is theirs, not the giver's, and urges the well-off to share.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Says Christians are not strangers to political life and urges public engagement for justice and peace.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Recalls and endorses the denunciation of economic and financial mechanisms managed by the strongest economies that structurally favor their own interests while stifling weaker ones.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Describes marriage as an exclusive and indissoluble union.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Repeatedly criticizes unbridled consumerism and says development is not truly human if it increases consumption for some while shifting costs onto others.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Urges public resources to support mothers and families and priority for welcoming life where birth rates are falling; no explicit financial incentives.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Categorically rejects antisemitism as sowing hatred and death.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Calls on governments to invest in the family founded on marriage of a man and a woman.

religion-illusion.rationale: Proclaims faith as truth and criticizes closing society to the transcendent.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Presents Catholic social teaching as criticizing both unlimited competition and collectivist projects, and as a response to the crisis of the great ideological systems.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Warns that the disappearance of first-hand Holocaust accounts leads to distorted rewriting of the past and calls for preserving memory.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Laments prisoners held for political reasons.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Says faith does not impose itself through coercion and asks all states to guarantee full religious freedom.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Lists colonialism among injustices requiring restorative justice.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Calls for shared responsibility and citizen initiative and says just ways begin from the ground up.

assisted-dying.rationale: Calls euthanasia a gravely wrong denial of the right to life and a deceptive form of compassion; urges palliative care.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Keeps the right of self-defense in the strictest sense and does not call for abolishing armies.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Says no just society endures unless law, and not arbitrary individual will, remains sovereign.

racial-franchise.rationale: Teaches equal dignity and rejects discrimination by ethnic origin.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Categorically rejects antisemitism and endorses equal dignity regardless of religious origin.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Denounces concentration of economic power in a few hands and concentration of digital power that evades public oversight.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Says faith must not cost a person their contribution to society and that the state should recognize and protect the religious dimension.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Backs an effective, just and humane criminal justice system and law enforcement.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Says almsgiving does not absolve authorities of their responsibility or the duty of government institutions to care for the poor, and criticizes the view that caring for the poor is not the state's job.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Explicitly leaves the right to self-defense in the strictest sense standing.

family-wage.rationale: Endorses the right to a fair wage for oneself and one's family and wages proportionate to the needs of workers and their families.

person-over-state.rationale: Says dignity precedes any concession by the State and takes precedence over all utility; endorses condemnation of states that exalt themselves above the person.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Says freedom should recognize and protect the religious dimension of the person and law should serve the whole person.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: States that armed force should be used only as a last resort in legitimate self-defense and calls just-war theory outdated.

future-generations.rationale: Says justice includes responsibility toward future generations and that progress must not compromise the living conditions of those who follow.

arms-reduction.rationale: Calls for disarmament, criticizes the arms race and rearmament and backs the nuclear weapons ban treaty as important.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Calls for respect for treaties and transparency of diplomatic action.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Laments that private militias and criminal networks end the State's monopoly on the use of force.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Calls for ethical scrutiny of international economic mechanisms that favor strong economies and for a world truly governed for everyone.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Grounds human dignity and rights in a dignity that belongs to every human being by their existence and critiques projects to transcend the human condition.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Says every sincere religious quest holds a reflection of the one divine Mystery, while proclaiming Christ; not a claim that all religions teach one truth.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Says belief that nuclear deterrence is indispensable is erroneous and welcomes the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Urges migrants to learn the language and respect the laws of the host country, as a duty alongside the host society's responsibilities; not a legal requirement.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Laments that tribunals dealing with war crimes are weakened or bypassed.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Says respect for dignity precludes even the death penalty after trial and torture and cruel punishment.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Affirms the universal destination of goods, including natural resources; does not state a compensation duty on those who appropriate them.

self-ownership.rationale: Rejects the conviction that man is the sole author of himself, his life and society.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Says a law's greatness is not mere formal enactment but whether it stands before the dignity of the person.

notes: Only his own words as pope (from May 2025) were used; no statement of Catholic doctrine in general was treated as his position unless he repeated or endorsed it in his own texts. Many passages in Magnifica Humanitas and Dilexi te recall predecessors; they count only where he presents them as his own teaching. His pre-papal positions as Robert Prevost (US immigration reposts, Peruvian politics) were not used as answers because the reposts are not his own statements. Several answers (same-sex marriage, reduce-immigration, open-borders) rest on statements about adjacent matters rather than a direct statement on the exact point, and are marked medium or low.
